properties.decision: UNDECIDED, and recorded as BRAINSTORMING rather than as a proposal — Anthony's own framing, 2026-07-25, thinking out loud. His starting doubt is the right one and had not been written down: claiming a cluster of nodes says nothing about the REPOSITORY, and if the design and the code share one repo, two people working different clusters still collide in git even when they never touch the same node. FOUR IDEAS AS HE PUT THEM. (1) reflow2 REPLACES git — the graph defines who may touch what, and git becomes an internal implementation detail. (2) The graph is a set of TEMPORARY LOCAL repos, pushed upstream only once work is done and no conflicts exist. (3) Each session opens a TEMPORARY WORKTREE BRANCH holding an identical copy of the graph; the person works there, then reflow2's own merge reconciles the copy back and the temporary is deleted. (4) A WEBSOCKET pushing every change to every user, giving live simultaneous collaboration. WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, and it matters for ranking them: the collision is in the export FILE, not in the graph, and reflow2 already answers file-level collision semantically — BL-80's three-way merge compares per node and per property against the common ancestor and mints each real conflict as a Question with a deterministic id, and `--merge`/`--merge-apply` run it without a server. So idea 3 is not new machinery; it is mostly a PROCEDURE over machinery that exists, and a git worktree already gives each person their own checkout with its own `.reflow2/graph` (the store lock is per-directory). The missing piece is small and specific: git supports per-path merge drivers — this repo already uses `merge=union` for COORD.md — so registering the design export with a driver that calls reflow2's own merge would make two people working different clusters merge automatically, and make a genuine overlap arrive as a Question instead of as conflict markers in a 500KB JSON file. Idea 2 is idea 3 with extra steps, since git branches are already local until pushed. Idea 1 would make reflow2 a version-control system, contradicts dec:repo-file-embedded and req:persistence, and would have to reinvent what it currently inherits for free. Idea 4 is the simultaneity road already held open by dec:central-host and BL-99, with the counter-argument recorded there: this tool's loop is deliberate and attributable rather than live.
properties.name: OPEN — how are two people's simultaneous edits kept apart: worktrees, temporary repos, or a live channel?
properties.rationale: Held as brainstorming on purpose. Anthony called it thinking out loud, and the first honest thing to do with four ideas is to write them down as four ideas rather than pick one and start building — which is precisely the practice dec:exploratory-staging is about. Two notes for whoever takes it up. The ranking above is a finding, not a decision: it says which ideas are cheap and which are large, and the cheap one is testable this week by two people on one design without a line of new Rust. And the doubt that started it should survive into whatever gets built — a claim on a cluster of nodes is not a claim on a repository, so any answer here has to say what happens to the CODE two people are writing beside the design, not only what happens to the graph.
